# std.ffi

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

The C boundary: raw pointers, C memory, and C strings.

`Ptr<T>` is a raw address: it has no ownership or lifetime, and the
collector never traces it. Reading, writing, allocating, and freeing
through raw pointers are foreign operations: they require `unsafe` and
contribute the `Foreign` effect. `T` is a scalar or a `repr c` struct.

## Types

### `Ptr`

```badger
pub extern type Ptr<T>
```

A raw C address of a `T`.

```

```

## Functions

### `alloc`

```badger
fn alloc<T>(count: Int) -> Ptr<T> !{Foreign}
```

Zeroed C memory for `count` values of `T` (free with `free`).

### `free`

```badger
fn free<T>(p: Ptr<T>) -> Unit !{Foreign}
```

### `null`

```badger
fn null<T>() -> Ptr<T>
```

The null pointer.

### `offset`

```badger
fn offset<T>(p: Ptr<T>, n: Int) -> Ptr<T> !{Foreign}
```

The address `n` elements after `p`.

### `read`

```badger
fn read<T>(p: Ptr<T>) -> T !{Foreign}
```

Read the `T` at `p` (copied into a managed value).

### `read_cstring`

```badger
fn read_cstring(p: Ptr<U8>) -> String !{Foreign}
```

Copy a NUL-terminated C string into managed text.

### `with_cstring`

```badger
fn with_cstring<R>(s: String, f: fn(Ptr<U8>) -> R) -> R !{Foreign}
```

A NUL-terminated copy of `s` in C memory for the duration of `f`
(the rooting/ownership adapter for passing text to C).

### `write`

```badger
fn write<T>(p: Ptr<T>, value: T) -> Unit !{Foreign}
```

Write `value` at `p` in C layout.
